subject: Feature-level unit economics & CAC payback — post-demo qualification
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amelia Torres <amelia@medora.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo — Feature-level unit economics & next steps

Hi Amelia —

Thanks again for hopping on today. Quick recap and the concrete asks we said we'd follow up on: 

1) Volume profile (please confirm):
   - Pilot: ~5M tokens / month (internal estimate)
   - Month 3 target: 20–30M tokens / month
   - Steady-state: 40–60M tokens / month (if feature adoption matches expectation)

2) Budget signal / target $/1M tokens: you mentioned a mid-point budget range today — can you confirm a target band you’d be comfortable with (e.g., $200–$350 / 1M tokens)?

3) Unit economics asks we will send:
   - $/feature breakdown (we’ll map tokens per feature + typical calls/day)
   - CAC payback scenarios (3, 6, 9, 12 month models) using your trial->paid conversion assumptions
   - Margin sensitivity vs inference cost (how end-user price needs to move for target gross margins)

4) Technical constraints: data residency & SOC2 are required for procurement — we have SOC2 evidence and regional routing options; I’ll attach the relevant docs.

Attached: medora_unit_econ_workbook.xlsx (workbook + token assumptions), demo-recording.mp4 (30m recording).

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the monthly volume bands and a target $/1M tokens range by end of week.
- We (Ben + Aditya) run a quick unit-econ deep-dive, send back a per-feature costing table and CAC payback sheet.
- If numbers look feasible, book a 60-min pricing deep-dive with engineering in the following week to validate technical levers (quantization, KV cache, batching) that change token unit cost.

If that plan looks good I’ll update the workbook with a few more feature examples and send through a one-page pricing summary.

Thanks —
Olga Petrov
Sr. Strategic Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: [medora_unit_econ_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB), demo-recording.mp4 (video, 30min)]

From: Amelia Torres <amelia@medora.ai>

Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@carelane.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 16:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo — Feature-level unit economics & next steps

Thanks Olga — good summary. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Volume: pilot is definitely 5M tokens / month (customer-facing pilot with 250 users). If pilot success metrics (15% weekly MAU increase on the feature) hit, we expect 25–45M tokens by month 6.

- Pricing target: at pilot we have limited budget. For steady-state we are aiming for $/1M token cost to be roughly $220–$300 to hit our internal product margin targets. We can stretch to $320 for a hosted, fully-managed solution if the SLA and data guarantees are there.

- Feature mix & tokens: the main candidate features for this proof are: 
   * Triage Assistant (conversational summaries) — ~140 tokens / interaction
   * Smart Intake (form auto-fill + context) — ~90 tokens / interaction
   * Patient FAQ (light reranking + retrieval) — ~60 tokens / interaction

- CAC / payback: our finance lead wants <9 months payback on incremental CAC for this feature set.

- Compliance: SOC2 is required; data residency in US-east preferred.

Happy to have Ben and Aditya model this. If you can include an assumed conversion lift per feature (we’re expecting +8–12% conversion into paid tiers from trials driven by Triage Assistant), that’ll help the payback math.

Best,
Amelia
Head of Product
Medora Health

--
Amelia Torres
Phone: +1 415 555 0199

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo — Feature-level unit economics & next steps

Folks — working notes to use for the workbook update (internal only):

1) Baseline hosted unit-cost assumptions (estimates per 1M tokens, production mix):
   - No caching, standard quant: $360 / 1M tokens (small-batch, low reuse)
   - With KV/prefix caching and batching optimization: ~$280 / 1M tokens
   - Dedicated + 12mo commit + int8 quantization: ~$185–$210 / 1M tokens (depends on sequence length and batching)

2) Per-feature mapping (use token-per-interaction * expected calls/day * users):
   - Triage Assistant: 140 tokens x 50 calls/day x 250 pilot users ≈ 1.75M tokens/day → pilot scale guidance: 52.5M tokens/mo (this is high; use limited call window assumption)
   - Smart Intake: 90 tokens x 15 calls/day x 250 users ≈ 3.375M tokens/mo
   - Patient FAQ: 60 tokens x 20 calls/day x 250 users ≈ 3M tokens/mo

   Note: those numbers suggest the pilot token footprint can blow past 5M if the usage pattern is optimistic. Recommend we model conservative usage: 10% of estimated calls initially.

3) CAC payback framing (3 scenarios):
   - Conservative: conversion uplift 5%, ARPU add $8/mo → payback ~12–14 months at hosted $/1M=280
   - Base: conversion uplift 8%, ARPU add $12/mo → payback ~7–9 months at hosted $/1M=280
   - Aggressive: conversion uplift 12%, ARPU add $18/mo → payback ~4–6 months at dedicated $/1M=200

4) Margin sensitivity: to achieve 50% gross margin on feature revenue, target unit-cost needs to be <= $240 / 1M tokens assuming current pricing plan (we’ll compute exact breakpoints in workbook).

5) Risk notes for the deep-dive:
   - Sequence length dominates cost for Triage Assistant (summaries).
   - Retrieval + reranking increases token counts when hits are low — recommend instrumentation to observe token-per-call in pilot.

Action items (internal):
- Olga: send updated workbook to Amelia with two named scenarios (pilot conservative / pilot base) and a one-pager that shows the CAC payback math for 3/6/9/12 months.
- Aditya: prep a 45-min engineering session to show cost levers (quantization impact, prefix caching, batching) and to validate the feasibility of our dedicated pricing numbers.

Ben
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amelia Torres <amelia@medora.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo — Feature-level unit economics & next steps

Amelia — thanks for the quick note and the budget band. I updated the attached workbook with 2 scenario pages ("Pilot — conservative" and "Pilot — base") plus a one-page CAC/payback summary. Highlights in the one-pager: 

- Pilot conservative: assumes 10% of modeled calls, results in ~4.8M tokens/mo; estimated $/1M tokens = $300 (hosted) → 11–13 month payback at 5% conversion uplift.
- Pilot base: assumes 35% of modeled calls, ~18M tokens/mo; estimated $/1M tokens = $255 (hosted w/ caching) → 6–8 month payback at 8% conversion uplift.
- Dedicated option: with a 12mo commit we can get to ~$200 / 1M tokens; that reduces payback to ~4–6 months in the base case.

I also added a simple sensitivity table that shows required end-user price per feature to hit 40%, 50% and 60% gross margin bands given the token-cost buckets above.

Next steps: 
- Please confirm which pilot scenario you want us to model in the contract example (conservative/base).
- If base, we propose scheduling the 45-min engineering deep-dive (Aditya + infra) next Tue or Wed (I’ll send calendar options).
- Also confirm whether SOC2 evidence and regional routing to us-east are sufficient for procurement; I attached a short SOC2 extract.

I attached the workbook again (medora_unit_econ_workbook.xlsx) and the one-pager PDF (included inside the workbook).

Thanks — looking forward to your confirmation.

Olga Petrov
Sr. Strategic Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: [medora_unit_econ_workbook.xlsx (updated), demo-recording.mp4]
